## Triage: first grade, `bug` · `security` · `priority:p1` · `domain:ui` · `area:access`, into `pm:queue`. The header action's click goes through the ActionRunner, and an omitted type means `url` there too

Triage seat (seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-12T22:54Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Why p1 and `security`:** ruling A+ on objectstack-ai/objectui#12191 says the scheme set "is stated once in the contract and the runtime fulfils exactly that". This handler keeps its own grammar. It navigates to a target class the contract and `classifyNavigationTarget` both refuse, and it fails on one the contract admits. Unlike objectstack's contract cards, the runtime guard here is the one that is missing. This is a tightening, so it does not escalate.
- **Direction, the card's own:**
  - The `url` click goes through the `ActionRunner`, which owns the type registry and `classifyNavigationTarget`, as every other header action already does. ⛔ No scheme list in `DashboardRenderer.tsx`.
  - An omitted `actionType` means `url` at the click, as `headerActionDefs` and the contract door read it.
  - The card's four pins, on a real render.
- **Not blocked:** the runner's classification is on `main` today, so this does not wait for objectstack's #23077.
- Triage: lands in `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx` (`domain:ui`); rationale: one handler joins the one runner.

Claim: PM loop round 3 (triage `6134181226`: the header action's click goes through the ActionRunner, which owns the type registry and `classifyNavigationTarget`, ⛔ no scheme list in `DashboardRenderer.tsx`; an omitted `actionType` means `url` at the click too; ruling A+ `6121792024` on objectui#12191)

File surface: the dashboard header action's click, read on objectui `main` `9f282ef` at 2026-10-12T23:58Z (stop on breach; explain in the report):
- **The handler:** `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx`. Its header action click handles `actionType === 'url'` itself (`location.assign` for `^https?://` or a leading `//`, else `history.pushState`), and returns with "Header action missing actionType/actionUrl" when `actionType` is omitted. The same file's `headerActionDefs` already builds `type: actionType || 'url'`.
- **The runner, read and reused:** `@object-ui/core`'s `ActionRunner` and its `classifyNavigationTarget`. ⛔ Not changed unless the dev measures a gap there, which stops and reports.
- Co-located tests (the card's four pins on a real render), and `.changeset/12275-dashboard-header-action-runner.md` (`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` `patch`).
- ⛔ No scheme list, regex or URL grammar of its own in `DashboardRenderer.tsx`; no new prop, spec key, export or i18n key.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: default tier — dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui: "no path-derived mandate"`
Clause-②: no
Clause-② reason: the runtime is brought onto the contract's own set, in both directions. The contract text: objectstack `packages/spec/src/ui/navigation-target.ts` admits "an address that opens with one of ADMITTED_SCHEMES — `http://`, `https://` or `mailto:`" and refuses "a protocol-relative `//host`"; `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts` declares `actionType: WidgetActionTypeSchema.optional()`, and objectstack's `validateDashboardActionRefs` reads an omitted type as `url`. So refusing `//host` and a bare relative value is a narrowing to that text, and admitting `mailto:` and an omitted type removes refusals the text already denies. Nothing published is widened; an at-tier contract review runs before the queue.
Responsibility: `objectui's dashboard renderer (@object-ui/plugin-dashboard DashboardRenderer), whose header action click keeps its own url grammar and bypasses the ActionRunner | the ActionRunner's classifyNavigationTarget already fulfils the contract's set for every other action (ruling A+ on objectui#12191) | every viewer of a dashboard whose author declares a header action; a //host target navigates off-site today (read from source, not executed in a browser)`
Thread-read: 6134181226
Serial constraints cleared: read at 2026-10-12T23:58Z on objectui `main` `9f282ef`. No open PR touches `DashboardRenderer.tsx` or the runner (open: objectui#12253, #12280, #12281). `DashboardRenderer.tsx` last changed on `main` today with seat 2's objectui#12265 (`e8fc452`), now landed. This seat's in-flight objectui#12274 (`app-shell` flow toast) shares no file.

## Landed: objectui PR #12284 → `main` `74964ad` · `domain:ui` seat 1 · `session_01CsyMRsFJBKNEMa4oPY1b5z` · 2026-10-13T00:54Z

- Merged through the merge queue. This card closed `completed` by the PR's `Fixes #12275`.
- **Landed by content, not by sha:** all 4 of the PR's files on `main` `74964ad` are blob-identical to the head the contract review judged, `e89a1e9` (record `6135411972`, PASS, nothing escalated).
- `pm:dispatched` was removed and read back. `domain:ui`, `area:access`, `security`, the type and the priority stay.
- The changeset (`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` `patch`) rides the next objectui release.
- **Behaviour now on `main`:** a dashboard header action of type `url`, or of no declared type, goes through the action runner. The runner's `classifyNavigationTarget` decides what the click may open, the same answer every other `url` action gets (ruling A+ on objectui#12191).
  - `//host`, a bare relative value and any foreign scheme are refused at the click. Under the console the runner's error toast reports the refusal.
  - `mailto:` opens in place.
  - An omitted `actionType` runs as `url`.
  - An `https://` target opens in a new tab under the console.
  - An in-app path still navigates in the app.
- **The spec door** (objectstack-ai/objectstack#23101, open) is unchanged by this landing. When it lands, the door and the click refuse the same set.
- **Three pre-existing notes stay as Acceptance notes on the PR, none filed (carrier: none):**
  - a provider-less `form` / `navigation` header action does not follow the runner's `redirect`;
  - two header actions sharing one `actionUrl` register under one name;
  - `modalHandler` / `scriptHandlers` stay installed on the shared provider runner.
